# Writing Plan — gen-depth-fingerprint
# Depth Fingerprinting of Recursive LLM Generation Chains
# Created: 2026-05-15

##############################################################################
# 1. Submission Target
##############################################################################

submission:
  primary:
    venue: EMNLP 2026 ARR
    deadline: 2026-05-25
    page_limit: "8 pages (long) + unlimited appendix"
    template: acl.sty
    special_requirements:
      - Limitations section (mandatory)
      - Ethics Statement
      - ARR submission format
    note: "D012: 主投 EMNLP ARR，DDL 仅剩 10 天，全速推进"
  fallback:
    - venue: AAAI 2027
      deadline: 2026-08-02
    - venue: ICLR 2027
      deadline: 2026-09-24
    - venue: NAACL 2027 ARR
      deadline: 2026-10-16

##############################################################################
# 2. One-Sentence Contribution
##############################################################################

one_sentence: >
  We formulate ordinal depth estimation for recursive LLM generation chains,
  showing that distributional features exhibit differential depth response
  (central-tendency drifts, shape remains stationary), yielding a 7-feature
  ensemble that reliably classifies generation depth (LOGO F1=0.79) across
  6 generators / 3 model families (including 7B+ scale).

##############################################################################
# 3. Claim-Evidence Map
##############################################################################

claims:
  C1_depth_discriminability:
    claim: >
      Distributional features under a held-out reference model classify
      generation depth (gen-0/gen-1/gen-2+) with macro-F1 significantly
      above chance, generalizing across unseen generators.
    evidence:
      - exp_id: plan-002-eval
        metric: "LOGO avg macro-F1 = 0.8037"
      - exp_id: plan-002-eval
        metric: "Leave-one-family-out Δ = +0.0107 (Pythia vs non-Pythia)"
      - exp_id: plan-015-v2
        metric: "Bootstrap CI [0.786, 0.799], p<0.001 vs all baselines"
      - exp_id: plan-013
        metric: "Length not a confound (|ρ|<0.14, normalized trends preserved)"
      - exp_id: plan-014
        metric: "6-gen LOGO F1=0.7886 (incl. Qwen3-8B), held-out F1=0.69, scale-invariant signal"
    tables: [Table 1, Table 2]
    figures: [Fig 2, Fig 3]

  C2_differential_response:
    claim: >
      Central-tendency/diversity features (entropy_mean, TTR, hapax_ratio) drift
      monotonically with depth; shape features (entropy_std, tail_decay) remain
      near-stationary. Full 7-feature set significantly outperforms surface-only
      and reference-only subsets.
    evidence:
      - exp_id: plan-001-fix
        metric: "full(0.82) > surface(0.76) > reference(0.72), CI non-overlapping"
      - exp_id: plan-002
        metric: "Drift direction consistent across all 6 generators (incl. 8B)"
      - exp_id: plan-002-eval
        metric: "full(0.80) > ref(0.75) = surf(0.75), McNemar p≈0"
      - exp_id: plan-003
        metric: "3 cross-family ref models: LOGO F1 0.80-0.82, drift direction consistent"
    tables: [Table 2]
    figures: [Fig 1]

  C3_downstream_negative:
    claim: >
      Depth-aware data curation does NOT improve downstream CLM quality.
      Data quantity dominates depth composition. Depth fingerprinting is
      diagnostic, not curative.
    status: NEGATIVE FINDING — report honestly
    evidence:
      - exp_id: plan-004-v2
        metric: "all(2.335) < size_matched(2.367) < depth01(2.387) ≈ binary_filtered(2.389)"
      - exp_id: plan-004-v2
        metric: "15/15 runs, cross-seed variance <0.002"
    tables: [Table 3]
    figures: [Fig 4]
    framing_note: >
      DO NOT hide or spin. Frame as: "We tested whether depth-aware curation
      improves downstream quality. It does not. The primary determinant is data
      quantity, not depth composition. This positions depth fingerprinting as a
      diagnostic tool for provenance characterization, not a curative tool for
      data selection."

##############################################################################
# 4. Paper Outline
##############################################################################

outline:
  abstract:
    length: "~200 words"
    structure: "five-sentence method (Farquhar)"
    key_points:
      - "We formulate ordinal depth estimation beyond binary detection"
      - "Why hard: existing detectors offer only real-vs-synthetic, no depth signal"
      - "How: 7 distributional features exhibiting differential depth response"
      - "Evidence: LOGO F1=0.79 across 6 generators / 3 families (incl. 7B+), p<0.001 vs baselines"
      - "Honest negative: depth-aware curation does not improve downstream quality"
    headline_note: >
      The paper_framing.md headline template contains "Z% downstream" placeholder.
      UPDATE to negative-finding wording: "...however, depth-aware data curation
      does not improve downstream model quality over random subsampling,
      positioning depth estimation as a diagnostic rather than curative tool."
    reviewer_concerns_covered: []

  introduction:
    length: "~1.5 pages"
    key_points:
      - "Problem: web data increasingly contains recursive LLM-generated text of unknown provenance depth"
      - "Gap: binary detectors cannot distinguish gen-1 from gen-2+, forcing all-or-nothing filtering"
      - "Our formulation: ordinal depth estimation as a new task (genuinely novel)"
      - "Core finding: differential depth response — level/diversity features drift, shape features are stationary"
      - "Practical consequence: 7-feature ensemble LOGO F1=0.79, reliable across unknown generators (incl. 7B+)"
      - "Honest reporting: downstream curation does not benefit (diagnostic, not curative)"
      - "Contributions list (3 items matching the 3 claims)"
    evidence:
      - exp_id: plan-015-v2  # headline numbers
      - exp_id: plan-002-eval  # LOGO result
    reviewer_concerns_covered: [RC8]
    notes:
      - "Must explicitly state contribution is empirical/conceptual, not methodological (D006+D007)"
      - "Connect to OOD detection literature in framing paragraph (RC8)"
      - "Do NOT overclaim 'dual dynamics' — use 'differential depth response' (D007)"

  related_work:
    length: "~1 page"
    organization: # see literature_strategy section below
      - subsection: "AI-Generated Text Detection"
        papers: [detectgpt, gltr, dna_gpt, binoculars, fast_detectgpt, ld_score, intrinsic_dimension, diveye, generator_barrier, feat_aug_transformer, reliable_detection, paraphrase_evades, detection_possibilities, grover, release_strategies, jawahar_survey]
        angle: "Binary detection only — no depth estimation capability. Single-score baselines show high cross-generator variance."
      - subsection: "Model Collapse and Iterative Generation"
        papers: [self_consuming_mad, curse_of_recursion, strong_model_collapse, model_collapse_avoidable, broken_telephone, markovian_chains]
        angle: "Training-loop collapse theory; iterative generation distortion. We study inference-chain depth without retraining."
      - subsection: "Vocabulary Diversity and Stylometry"
        papers: [curious_decline, writing_diversity, nucleus_sampling, mapping_llm_science, monitoring_ai_review, stamatatos_survey, koppel_authorship, uchendu_attribution]
        angle: "Diversity decline documented but not used for depth estimation. Our surface features are stylometric in nature."
      - subsection: "Data Quality and Provenance"
        papers: [dsir, qurating, ccnet, watermark_llm, synthid_text, aaronson_watermark, chainwash, min_k_percent, ood_baseline]
        angle: "Quality scoring/watermarking for data curation. Depth fingerprint complements these as provenance signal."
    reviewer_concerns_covered: [RC1, RC8]

  method:
    length: "~1.5 pages"
    subsections:
      - name: "Task Formulation"
        content: "Ordinal depth estimation: given text x, predict depth class {gen-0, gen-1, gen-2+}"
        length: "~0.25 page"
      - name: "Generation Chain Construction"
        content: "6 generators (Pythia-2.8B, Pythia-1B, OLMo-2-1B, Qwen3-1.7B, Qwen3-0.6B, Qwen3-8B), 3 families, ~1000 seeds × 5 depths, continuation prompt, temp=0.7/top_p=0.9/max_tokens=256"
        evidence: [mvp-001, plan-002, plan-014]
        length: "~0.25 page"
      - name: "Feature Extraction"
        content: "7 features: 4 reference-model (entropy_mean/std/max, tail_decay) + 3 surface (TTR, hapax_ratio, entropy_min). Reference model = Pythia-410M."
        length: "~0.5 page"
      - name: "Evaluation Protocol"
        content: "Leave-one-generator-out (LOGO) cross-validation. XGBoost classifier. Bootstrap CI (n=1000). McNemar test for feature ablation."
        length: "~0.5 page"
    reviewer_concerns_covered: [RC2, RC4, RC6]

  results:
    length: "~2 pages"
    subsections:
      - name: "Depth Classification Performance (C1)"
        content: "6-gen LOGO F1=0.79, per-generator breakdown (0.69-0.85), family-out Δ=+0.01. Gen-0 near-perfect (F1=0.95), gen-1 vs gen-2+ harder. Qwen3-8B held-out F1=0.69 (cross-scale gap)."
        evidence: [plan-002-eval, plan-015-v2, plan-014]
        tables: [Table 1]
        figures: [Fig 2]
        length: "~0.5 page"
      - name: "Differential Depth Response (C2)"
        content: "Feature drift patterns. entropy_mean/TTR/hapax drift monotonically. entropy_std/tail_decay near-stationary. Feature complementarity: full > surface = reference."
        evidence: [plan-001-fix, plan-002, plan-003]
        tables: [Table 2]
        figures: [Fig 1]
        length: "~0.5 page"
      - name: "Comparison with Detection Baselines"
        content: "7-feature vs Avg-LogProb (+3.9pp, p<0.001), FastDetectGPT (+6.7pp), LD-Score, Binoculars. Key advantage: tight CI vs high variance of single detectors."
        evidence: [plan-015-v2]
        figures: [Fig 3]
        length: "~0.5 page"
      - name: "Downstream Utility — Negative Finding (C3)"
        content: "Depth-aware curation does not improve CLM quality. all(2.335) < size_matched(2.367) < depth01(2.387). Quantity dominates composition. Diagnostic not curative."
        evidence: [plan-004-v2]
        tables: [Table 3]
        figures: [Fig 4]
        length: "~0.5 page"
    reviewer_concerns_covered: [RC1, RC2, RC10, RC11]

  discussion:
    length: "~0.5 page"
    key_points:
      - "Why shape features are stationary: determined by sampling mechanism and architecture, invariant to input content drift (speculative, explicitly flagged)"
      - "Practical implications: risk-stratified data curation (flag gen-2+ for review, keep gen-1)"
      - "Honest framing of C3: negative finding has positive information value — rules out depth-based filtering as curation strategy"
      - "Connection to model collapse literature: inference chains show similar distributional drift without retraining"
    reviewer_concerns_covered: [RC3, RC8]

  limitations:
    length: "~0.25 page (mandatory for EMNLP; good practice for AAAI)"
    items:
      - "Generators up to 8B tested (plan-014); depth signal exists at scale but cross-scale transfer gap (8B held-out F1=0.69 vs ≤2.8B 0.76-0.85). Frontier models (70B+) untested."
      - "Single prompt type (continuation); elaboration/rewriting chains not yet tested (plan-005 pending)"
      - "Lab-constructed single-model chains; real web contamination involves diverse generators per step"
      - "Negative downstream result tested on CLM only; other downstream tasks not evaluated"
      - "3-class granularity; finer-grained depth may be possible for non-paraphrastic chains"
    reviewer_concerns_covered: [RC3, RC4, RC5, RC6, RC9]

  conclusion:
    length: "~0.25 page"
    key_points:
      - "Restate contributions: task formulation, empirical characterization, honest negative on downstream"
      - "Report realistic performance range (0.69-0.85 per-generator, 0.79 LOGO average)"
      - "Future work: frontier-scale generators, mixed-generator chains, prompt type diversity"

##############################################################################

##############################################################################

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as ticker
import numpy as np

# --- Data (ordered bottom-to-top for forest plot) ---
methods = [
    'Binoculars',
    'FastDetectGPT',
    'LD-Score (corrected)',
    'Avg-LogProb',
    '7-Feature Ensemble',
]
f1 =       [0.579,  0.6269, 0.7212, 0.7653, 0.798]
ci_lower = [0.405,  0.511,  0.588,  0.616,  0.786]
ci_upper = [0.664,  0.762,  0.770,  0.820,  0.799]

n = len(methods)
y_pos = np.arange(n)

# Okabe-Ito palette (colorblind-safe)
OI_BLUE    = '#0072B2'
OI_ORANGE  = '#E69F00'
OI_GREEN   = '#009E73'
OI_VERMIL  = '#D55E00'
OI_PURPLE  = '#CC79A7'

colors = [OI_PURPLE, OI_VERMIL, OI_GREEN, OI_ORANGE, OI_BLUE]

# --- Figure ---
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 4.5))  # ~4:3

for i in range(n):
    is_ensemble = (methods[i] == '7-Feature Ensemble')
    marker = 'o'
    ms = 9 if is_ensemble else 7
    mfc = colors[i] if is_ensemble else 'white'
    mec = colors[i]
    lw = 2.2 if is_ensemble else 1.6
    zorder = 5 if is_ensemble else 4

    ax.plot(f1[i], y_pos[i], marker=marker, markersize=ms,
            markerfacecolor=mfc, markeredgecolor=mec, markeredgewidth=1.5,
            zorder=zorder, clip_on=False)
    ax.hlines(y_pos[i], ci_lower[i], ci_upper[i],
              colors=colors[i], linewidth=lw, zorder=zorder - 1)

    # Right-side annotation: F1 [CI_low, CI_up]
    label = f'{f1[i]:.3f}  [{ci_lower[i]:.3f}, {ci_upper[i]:.3f}]'
    ax.text(0.87, y_pos[i], label, va='center', ha='left', fontsize=9,
            fontfamily='monospace', color='#333333')

# Chance level (3-class)
ax.axvline(x=1/3, color='#999999', linestyle='--', linewidth=1.0, zorder=1)
ax.text(1/3 + 0.008, n - 0.15, 'chance', fontsize=8, color='#999999', va='top')

# Light grid
ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(ticker.MultipleLocator(0.1))
ax.grid(axis='x', color='#E0E0E0', linewidth=0.5, zorder=0)
ax.set_axisbelow(True)

# Axes
ax.set_yticks(y_pos)
ax.set_yticklabels(methods, fontsize=11)
ax.set_xlabel('LOGO Macro-F1', fontsize=11)
ax.set_xlim(0.25, 0.86)
ax.set_ylim(-0.5, n - 0.5)

# Remove top/right spines
ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)

# Title (optional, can remove for paper)
# ax.set_title('Baseline Comparison', fontsize=12, pad=10)

plt.tight_layout()

out_dir = '/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0514_3/projects/gen-depth-fingerprint/figures/paper'
fig.savefig(f'{out_dir}/fig3_baseline_comparison.pdf', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=300)

\section{Related Work}

\subsection{AI-Generated Text Detection}

A large body of work addresses binary classification of machine-generated text.
Statistical approaches exploit token-level probability signals:
\cite{gltr} use token rank histograms under a reference model,
\cite{detectgpt} identify machine text through negative log-probability curvature,
and \cite{fast_detectgpt} accelerate this via conditional probability curvature.
\cite{binoculars} contrast perplexity ratios between two similar models,
while \cite{dna_gpt} measure n-gram divergence after re-generation.
More recent work extends these ideas:
\cite{ld_score} introduce character-distribution signatures orthogonal to perplexity,
\cite{intrinsic_dimension} leverage embedding-space intrinsic dimensionality,
and \cite{diveye} capture token surprisal diversity patterns.
Learned approaches include generator-specific discriminators \cite{grover},
feature-augmented transformers for cross-domain transfer \cite{feat_aug_transformer},
and disentangled representations for cross-generator generalization \cite{generator_barrier}.
Robustness analyses show that paraphrase attacks severely degrade detectors \cite{reliable_detection,paraphrase_evades},
though detection remains information-theoretically feasible whenever human and machine distributions are distinguishable \cite{detection_possibilities}.
\cite{jawahar_survey} and \cite{release_strategies} provide broader surveys.

These methods share a fundamental limitation: they produce a single binary score with no capacity for depth estimation.
When repurposed as ordinal depth predictors, individual detector scores exhibit high cross-generator variance (confidence intervals spanning 0.59--0.82 in our experiments), making them unreliable as standalone depth estimators.
Our reference-model entropy features are functionally NLL-based out-of-distribution scores \cite{ood_baseline}, drawing on the same signal backbone as DetectGPT and Binoculars.
The contribution is not the features themselves but rather the ordinal depth formulation, the empirical finding of differential depth response under recursive generation, and multi-feature complementarity that yields tight cross-generator consistency.

\subsection{Model Collapse and Iterative Generation}

Model collapse theory establishes that recursive training on synthetic data degrades generative quality.
\cite{curse_of_recursion} prove that iterative retraining causes irreversible distribution tail loss across VAEs, GMMs, and LLMs.
\cite{strong_model_collapse} show that even minimal synthetic data fractions suffice to trigger collapse,
\cite{self_consuming_mad} characterize precision--diversity trade-offs in autophagous loops,
and \cite{model_collapse_avoidable} demonstrate that data accumulation (rather than replacement) mitigates the effect.
These results concern \emph{training-loop} dynamics where model parameters change across iterations.
We study \emph{inference chains}: the same frozen model generates text recursively without retraining, yet distributional drift still accumulates.

Two concurrent works study iterative generation directly.
\cite{broken_telephone} analyze LLM paraphrasing and translation chains, showing that information distortion accumulates with depth and outputs converge toward attractor states---critically, the semantic-preservation constraint of paraphrasing bounds depth-distinguishable classes to approximately three.
\cite{markovian_chains} formalize this convergence, proving that iterative rephrasing chains either collapse to small cycle sets or continue producing novel sentences depending on temperature and initialization.
Both focus on \emph{paraphrastic} chains.
We study \emph{non-paraphrastic} continuation chains, where the absence of semantic anchoring permits richer depth signal, and formulate depth estimation as an explicit ordinal classification task rather than analyzing convergence behavior.

\subsection{Vocabulary Diversity and Stylometry}

Several studies document diversity decline in LLM-mediated text.
\cite{curious_decline} quantify lexical, syntactic, and semantic diversity loss across recursive fine-tuning iterations, finding particularly severe decline for creative tasks---the closest antecedent to our work, though they study training-loop effects rather than inference-chain drift and do not formulate depth estimation.
\cite{writing_diversity} show that LLM-assisted writing reduces inter-author diversity,
while \cite{mapping_llm_science} and \cite{monitoring_ai_review} estimate that 7--17\% of scientific papers and peer reviews contain substantial LLM-modified content.
\cite{nucleus_sampling} characterize neural text degeneration, proposing nucleus sampling whose truncation behavior shapes the distributional properties our features capture.

These works document diversity decline as a phenomenon but do not exploit it for depth classification.
Our surface features (type-token ratio, hapax ratio) are essentially stylometric, drawing on a long tradition of computational stylometry \cite{stamatatos_survey,koppel_authorship}.
\cite{uchendu_attribution} extend authorship attribution to neural text generator identification;
we further extend from \emph{source} attribution to \emph{depth} estimation, combining surface stylometric features with reference-model distributional features for complementary signal.

\subsection{Data Quality and Provenance}

Data curation pipelines increasingly rely on quality scoring to filter web-scale corpora.
\cite{ccnet} use language model perplexity for quality filtering,
\cite{dsir} apply importance resampling in n-gram feature space,
and \cite{qurating} employ LLM pairwise judgments for multi-dimensional quality assessment.
These methods score text quality but do not assess generation provenance or depth.

Watermarking offers an active provenance mechanism:
\cite{watermark_llm} embed statistical signals via green-list token biasing,
\cite{synthid_text} deploy production-scale watermarking,
and \cite{aaronson_watermark} propose pseudorandom function-based marking.
However, \cite{chainwash} demonstrate that multi-step rewriting chains reduce watermark detectability from 87.9\% to 4.86\% within five hops, motivating watermark-free approaches.
Depth fingerprinting complements both paradigms as a \emph{passive} provenance signal requiring no watermark embedding.
Methodologically, our probability-based features also connect to membership inference \cite{min_k_percent}, which analyzes token probability distributions for training set membership rather than generation depth.
